_comment: Inputs to the win-probability model, and the only part of it anyone edits.
These are the blue cells of the KU Volleyball 2026 Win Model workbook.
Win % = 1 / (1 + 10 ^ (-gap / scale)), gap = kansas + venue - opponent.
A gap of zero is exactly 50%, and each further 'scale' points multiply the
odds by ten. scale = 25 is tuned so the weakest opponent at home lands near
87% rather than 97%, which is closer to how often college volleyball produces
an upset. Raise it to flatten everything toward 50%, lower it to sharpen the
favourites.
A ranked team is not rated here at all. Its rating is read from the current
AVCA Coaches Poll on every scrape, through pollMap below, so it moves on its
own the Monday a new poll lands. The ratings in 'teams' are the fallback for
everyone the poll does not cover - which is most of the Big 12 - and those are
subjective estimates on a 0-100 scale, NOT an official system, anchored to the
Big 12 preseason coaches' poll of 11 Aug 2026. 'basis' records the reasoning.
A fallback is also capped at the rating of the poll's last-placed team, so a
stale number cannot leave a team that has dropped out of the poll rated above
the team still in it.
The fallbacks are the part that still needs a human, and they go stale: they
are preseason opinion about teams that have since played a season. Revisit
them when a Big 12 team's form clearly diverges from where it was picked.
The scrape reads this file; it never writes it.
Turns an AVCA poll line into a power rating:
rating = base + perShare * (points / (ballots * 25))
Poll points are divided by the most any team could have received, so the
map does not shift if the number of voting coaches changes. Ballots are
counted from the first-place votes, since every ballot carries exactly one.
base and perShare are a least-squares fit of this line to the six ranked
Big 12 ratings that were originally set by hand from the 14 Sep 2026 poll.
It reproduces all six within 1.3 points - Arizona St. 79.3 against 80, TCU
79.1 against 79, Colorado 75.0 against 74, Baylor 74.2 against 74, Kansas
72.7 against 72, BYU 71.7 against 73 - so switching to the poll changed
what the model says about a team hardly at all. What it changed is that the
numbers now move by themselves. On that poll the scale runs from 86.1 at
No. 1 to 71.5 at No. 25.

Arizona State.basis: AVCA No. 12 (7-2); picked 1st in Big 12 preseason

TCU.basis: AVCA No. 13 (6-2); picked 2nd in Big 12 preseason

Colorado.basis: AVCA No. 17 (8-0); picked 5th in Big 12 preseason

Baylor.basis: AVCA No. 18 (6-2); picked 4th in Big 12 preseason

Iowa State.basis: Picked 6th in Big 12 preseason; no longer receiving AVCA votes
